decisions.reason: The boost-rail rating and named 5V loads do not change the independently specified DCDC1 3.3V rail, whose same-message introduction already records its rating and loads.
Naming loads downstream of the MT3608 does not change the AXP2101 battery and system power path; its existing all-system-load coverage remains valid.
The boost-rail load and current specification does not alter the battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, part number, or unresolved pin order.
The 5V boost-rail specification does not change the established battery protection controller, thresholds, or DW01A protection components.
The source does not change the battery NTC terminal, connector, thermal-protection function, or controller.
The conditional mention of SK6812 supply voltage does not change how charge status is displayed or the dedicated charge-LED interface.
The boost-rail update does not change the standalone USB 3.3V supply; that Requirement already has a same-message MODIFY for the separate LDO and OR-ing clauses.
The rated current and load assignment of the 5V boost rail do not change the existing interboard connector partition, 5V pin, or 5V_EN signal.
The source allocates loads among power rails but does not add, remove, or reorganize any project board.
Identifying SPS30 and ZE08-CH2O as 5V loads does not itself specify or change the sensor-board connector fanout.
The source says SK6812 LEDs may use the 5V rail depending on the version, so their supply remains conditional and cannot be propagated as a definite MODIFY without a client decision.
The functional rating and load allocation of the boost rail do not necessarily change the existing BOM-readiness, part-number, or approved-component state.
